## What's new

The six planned items from the Roofoo Tools board.

- **More hotkeys** (#7). All can be changed in Help → Keyboard shortcuts.
  - **Shift+1 … Shift+0**: show only that layer (Floor 1, Floor 2, Wall 1–4, Shadows, Roofs, Lower walls, Special tiles). Press it again to get back the layers you had.
  - **Middle-click** a button in the layer bar above the map does the same.
  - **Backspace**: show every layer.
  - **F1–F6**: Tiles, Objects, Walkability, Automap, Level light and Roof hiding modes.
  - **Ctrl+1 … Ctrl+7**: the layer you work on (Floor 1, Floor 2, Wall 1–4, Shadows).
  - **Home**: zoom to 100%. **=** and **-** zoom a step in or out. Clicking the zoom figure in the status bar also goes to 100%.
- **Alt with the brush: first free layer** (#8). Alt+click or Alt+drag with the Paint tool puts each tile on the first empty layer of its kind there, as Alt does when pasting. When all the layers there are taken, it adds a wall or floor layer if the map has room (up to 4 walls and 2 floors); otherwise it replaces the tile on the active layer. Going over a cell twice in one stroke keeps it on the same layer. This also works with the Rectangle paint mode.
- **DT1 library and editor** (#9):
  - In the DT1 library, select one of the map's libraries ("In this map") and press **Delete**, or click "Remove it from the map…". It asks first and says how many placed tiles come from it.
  - **Edit a custom DT1**: select a DT1 of your mod, click this new button next to "Build a custom DT1", then tick tiles in any libraries to add them to it. Its own tiles stay as they are; the new ones get numbers no other library of the level uses.
  - In the DT1 editor, select tiles and press **Delete** (or click Delete…) to remove them. It asks first and warns when the open map uses them. Nothing is written until you save.
  - **Sort by number** puts the tiles in order of orientation, then main and sub index. Tiles that share a number keep their order, because that order matters in game.
- **Zoom in sharp steps** (#10). The mouse wheel now zooms in steps that keep every pixel sharp: 1/8×, 1/4×, 1/2×, 3/4×, 100%, 2×, 3×, 4×… Game view and Fit map land on a step too, so you always get back to exactly 100%. The zoom figure now counts screen pixels per game pixel, so 100% is as sharp as in game even with Windows display scaling. To zoom freely as before, turn on Preferences → Zoom smoothly.

## Fixes

- **Clone and Mirror pick free numbers** (#11). A tile cloned or mirrored in the DT1 editor no longer takes a number that another DT1 loaded with it already uses; the game would draw that other DT1's tile instead. It checks the open map's other libraries and every level type that lists the DT1. A mirrored wall faces the other way, so its number changes; when that number is taken, the wall gets a free sub index, and the note says so.
- **Moving objects is smooth** (#12). Dragging an object or an NPC path point follows the mouse sub-tile by sub-tile; before, it jumped a whole tile at a time. It also keeps the spot where you grabbed it instead of snapping its centre to the pointer. Each step of the drag no longer rebuilds the whole map, so it keeps up on big maps.
- After a paste or a brush stroke adds a layer, the layer bar now shows it straight away.
